glosses: To don (clothing, equipment, or the like).

examples.text: Why don't you put on your jacket. It's cold.
And Iacob vowed a vow, ſaying, If God will be with me, and will keepe me in this way that I goe, and will giue me bꝛead to eate, and raiment to put on.

glosses: To decorate or dress (something) onto another person or a surface.

examples.text: I put a coat on my daughter.
I put tinsel on the Christmas tree.

glosses: To fool, kid, deceive.

examples.text: She's putting on that she's sicker than she really is.
You must be putting me on.

glosses: To assume, adopt or affect; to behave in a particular way as a pretense.

examples.text: Why are you putting that silly voice on?
He's just putting on that limp -- his leg's actually fine.

glosses: To play (a recording).

examples.text: I'll put your favorite record on.
Can you put on The Sound of Music? I'd like to see it again.

glosses: To play (a recording) on (a sound system).

examples.text: I'll put blues on the stereo.
We usually put The Beatles on on my boombox.

glosses: To initiate cooking or warming, especially on a stovetop.

examples.text: I'll put on some coffee for everybody.

glosses: To perform for an audience.

examples.text: The actors put on a show last Saturday.
The actors will put "Macbeth" on only one more time.

glosses: To organize a performance for an audience.

examples.text: The theatre company is putting on "Into the Woods" this season.

glosses: To provide.

examples.text: Peterbough United have been playing at Lincoln, in something of a local derby. EMR has put on a six-car Class 158 as an additional train, to take 'Posh' fans home (Posh is the team's nickname, by the way).

glosses: To bet (money or other items) on (something).

examples.text: I put five pounds on that racehorse.

glosses: To assign or apply (something) to a target.

examples.text: The gang boss put some goons on the other gang.
The witch put a hex on me.
Carl has been put on the front desk for tonight's shift.

glosses: To give (someone) a role in popular media.

examples.text: I hope they put me on TV.
They put her on a billboard.

glosses: To set (movie, show, song, etc.) to play on a screen.

examples.text: I put SpongeBob on when the kid gets fussy.

glosses: To gain (weight).

examples.text: I put on at least five kilos over the holidays.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see put, on.

examples.text: He put the pen on the table.
Put it on the list.
The doctor put me on a diet.

glosses: To hurry up; to move swiftly forward.

examples.text: Sophia […] saw several horses coming after on full speed. This greatly alarmed her fears, and she called to the guide to put on as fast as possible.
